messages:
maya: CI red on nightly-gpu (h100 pool). failing test: tests/inference/test_quantized_end2end.py::test_streaming_chunked
maya: failure looks like a kernel launch error + driver mismatch in the logs. saw: 
```
  [2026-05-02 03:12:09] E cuda: kernel_launch: failed: invalid device function (err 8)
  [2026-05-02 03:12:09] E driver: host libcuda.so.1 (525.50) != container libcuda.so.1 (530.14)
  ```
maya: repro cmd in CI container: `docker run --gpus all -it --entrypoint /bin/bash ghcr.io/redwood/infer-nightly:gpu-2026-05-01` then `pytest tests/inference/test_quantized_end2end.py::test_streaming_chunked -k chunked -q`
maya: tagging in case someone on call can pick this up :eyes:

josh: thanks, looks like the usual host/container driver mismatch. which node image was this on?
maya: node: dgx-1a.h100-qt (ami-2026-04-28), job id 7201993, image digest sha256:abc123f...
linus: i can try a quick repro on a dev DGX, will run the same docker image. can you paste the small stack trace?
maya: pasted above, but also CI log shows `libdevice` PTX JIT fallback thrash and then kernel launch failure at attention_kernel.cu: line 243
sophie: if it's host driver older than container it fails at kernel symbol resolution. workaround: rebuild container with older libcuda symlink or use `--privileged` with host libs (not ideal).
ci-bot: rerun requested by @maya for job 7201993 — queued to h100-pool (attempt 2) :white_check_mark:
josh: while rerun goes, can we try a minimal cuda sample inside that image to surface mismatch quickly? e.g. run `./deviceQuery` from CUDA samples.
linus: ran deviceQuery on dgx. host driver 525.50, container reports 530.14 — mismatch confirmed. deviceQuery returns CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN on container build.
sophie: ok two mitigation paths: 1) pin container CUDA runtime to host driver (downgrade container to 525.x) or 2) update host driver cluster-side (needs infra change). which is faster?
josh: short-term: rebuild image to match 525.50 and push, trigger CI. long-term: infra needs driver standardization + CI should assert host/container compat on node startup.
maya: added a CI check in the failing PR to assert `nvidia-smi` versions and abort early — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/4321
maya: rerun (attempt 2) completed, still failing same error. logs identical. :frustrated:
linus: then we need a bisect — can someone try older nightly image? maybe regression in our compiled kernels (attention optimizations) between build abc123f and def456a.
josh: I'll queue a bisect across images from 2026-04-20..2026-05-01. ping me if you want me to stop when green.
sophie: also add a small reproducer C++ kernel that triggers the same path so we can test outside PyTorch to rule out hlo changes.
maya: created a small reproducer gist and attached to the PR. thanks all, will follow up with results from the bisect. :pray:
